name: Approach to the pubic symphysis
aliases: Pfannenstiel approach to the anterior pelvic ring
corridor: Pfannenstiel or inferior-midline laparotomy extension through the linea alba into the retropubic space, elevating rectus from the pubis while protecting the bladder and prostatic venous plexus

positioning.text: Position supine so the lower abdomen and pubic tubercles are in the field and the bladder can be catheterized.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the pubic tubercles, linea alba, and a line about two fingerbreadths proximal to the tubercles.

incision.text: Use a 5–10 cm horizontal Pfannenstiel cut about two fingerbreadths above the pubic tubercle, extended laterally as needed. If a midline laparotomy is already present, extend its inferior end instead.

superficial_interval.text: Identify the anterior rectus fascia, protect the spermatic cord or round ligament if the cut is carried laterally, locate the linea alba, and incise it longitudinally. Retract both rectus bellies laterally.

deep_interval.text: Bluntly develop the retropubic space, protecting the bladder and prostatic venous plexus. One rectus insertion is often avulsed by the injury; elevate remaining muscle subperiosteally past the pubic tubercle while keeping distal fascial continuity to reduce later hernia. A pointed Hohmann over the tubercle retracts muscle. Lateral dissection can reach the obturator foramen for forceps and the rami to the iliopectineal eminence, or be continued as a modified Stoppa.

layers.text: Skin, rectus fascia and linea alba, preperitoneal retropubic space, periosteum of the pubis, then the symphysis and superior rami.

structures_at_risk.text: The bladder, prostatic venous plexus, spermatic cord or round ligament, and later hernia if distal rectus fascia is sacrificed are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The retropubic space is the danger zone for the bladder and prostatic venous plexus. Stay preperitoneal proximally.

retraction_hazards.text: Do not avulse remaining distal rectus fascia. Inspect the Foley bag for blood before closure.

exposure.text: Shows the anterior pelvic ring for symphyseal plating and superior-ramus work, and can be carried laterally to the SI joint as a modified Stoppa.

limitations.text: The standard window is the anterior ring. Quadrilateral-surface and SI access require lateral Stoppa extension.

indications.text: Used for pubic-symphysis disruption or diastasis and for anterior-ring fractures including the superior rami.

closure.text: Irrigate, inspect the bladder and urine, and close the midline rectus incision and superficial tissues in layers.

complications.text: Complications include bladder injury, prostatic-plexus bleeding, hernia from lost distal rectus fascia, and peritoneal entry.

procedure_applications.condition: A pubic-symphysis disruption or anterior-ring fracture is plated through a Pfannenstiel window

questions.question: Where is a Pfannenstiel incision placed?
questions.answer: About two fingerbreadths proximal to the pubic tubercle, typically 5–10 cm.
